interpretation_rules.lower_bound: A variant whose mean API CPU over all its main points is below 0.95 core is reported as an RPS lower bound (client or latency limited), with API CPU per response as secondary metric, unless the pair is flagged by direction_under_client_limit, where it is the primary metric; never as a server capacity ratio. Classified once per variant.
interpretation_rules.direction_under_client_limit: Generator saturation is anchored to generator CPU in the static controls (static-pre before main, static after main; mean of all four). Static RPS is not used as a limit, because generator cost per response differs between the static Go server and uvicorn responses. If either side of a pair has mean generator CPU >= 0.9 x static generator CPU, the RPS direction of that pair is not reported as a server result; API CPU per response is then the primary metric. Generator CPU per response is reported per variant.
interpretation_rules.pair_ratio: The pair ratio is the measured throughput ratio with 20 closed-loop clients and memoized body verification on 2 generator CPUs; not a capacity ratio. A direction may be claimed only if the nominal interval excludes 0. The same rule applies to API CPU per response (comparisons[pair].api_cpu_us_per_response, same estimator). The primary metric of each pair is fixed in advance: RPS, or API CPU per response for pairs flagged by direction_under_client_limit; the other metric is descriptive and never replaces a null primary result. When neither side is a lower bound (API at least 0.95 core on both), the CPU interval mirrors the RPS interval and is not independent evidence. analyze.py records the decision per pair: primary_metric, primary_direction_claim_allowed, rps_direction_claim_allowed, cpu_compared_at_different_loads and cpu_interval_mirrors_rps.
interpretation_rules.redis: Redis gets 0.2 CPU and 1024 MiB on cpuset 1 (maxmemory 900mb, noeviction) as in series 3 and 7; series 8 has no view-cache variants, so Redis holds no pages. If Redis throttled time exceeds 1% of the measurement window in any point of a variant, that variant is reported as Redis-limited.
interpretation_rules.host_drift: The host is a cloud KVM VM with 8 vCPUs in two NUMA nodes (0-3 and 4-7); exclusive physical cores are not confirmed by the provider documentation, and zero steal does not exclude cache or memory-bandwidth contention. Per-point steal and softirq shares of CPUs 0-3 are reported and a point with steal above 1% of the window is flagged. Static controls before and after main are compared by RPS, generator CPU per response and API CPU per response; a difference above 10% in RPS or generator CPU per response flags the series as host-drifted, reported with the results. The per-round values of fastapi-msgspec (both sides of aa-get-fast and one side of the other two pairs, every round) are reported as an in-series drift trace. Per-response CPU values of this series are never set next to values of other series.
interpretation_rules.equal_load: After main and headroom, every measured variant runs two open-loop points at 400 offered RPS (GET), 30 s after a 15 s throughput warmup, order as listed then reversed. The rate follows matched-rate-rule.md: 0.7 x the minimum throughput smoke RPS of the measured variants on this server, rounded down to a multiple of 100, fixed before this protocol. API CPU per response at equal load is unpaired and reported descriptively (no interval) alongside the paired main-series value, which depends on load.
interpretation_rules.request_mix: Every tenth request (global counter) is a unique cold page from the pool, taken sequentially from offset 0 in the warmup run and from offset 25000 in the measurement run (pool 80000) of each point; an exhausted pool is a client error. Every variant serves this mix from PostgreSQL (CACHE_MODE=bypass, VIEW_CACHE=disabled). Static controls use only the hot page.
interpretation_rules.headroom: After main, the client 1/2/2/1 CPU sweep runs for fastapi-msgspec, plus two static controls.
interpretation_rules.path_disclosure: All three measured variants are the same application and process configuration: MsgspecRouter without output schema (msgspec-fastapi main through bench/router-main-shim), direct asyncpg queries, uvloop, one uvicorn worker. h11-httptools changes only --http (h11 to httptools); accesslog-off-on changes only the access log (--no-access-log on side A, the uvicorn default access log on side B, so B/A is the cost of the log). The access log is written by the uvicorn.access logger to the container stdout, collected by the Docker json-file logging driver. That collection runs in the containerd shim of the API container and in dockerd on the system CPUs, outside the API cgroup: it is not included in API CPU per response and is reported separately per point (log_pipeline in analyze.py, the per-process CPU of the shim and of dockerd; dockerd also serves the runner and the sampler, so only the difference between the sides of accesslog-off-on is attributable to the access log). Unbound kernel work queues are restricted to CPUs 4-7. Python logging writes to stdout synchronously: if the pipe were ever full, the event loop would wait and RPS would fall without API CPU rising, and the lower_bound rule then reports that variant as an RPS lower bound (mean API CPU below 0.95 core). A log written to a file or a remote collector costs differently.
interpretation_rules.series8: One stack: the API image built from Dockerfile-T (CPython 3.14.10, requirements-T.lock as in series 7 plus httptools 0.9.0, which uvicorn imports only with --http httptools), msgspec-fastapi main (commit in evidence/router-main.json) built on this server as one cp311-abi3 wheel and reached through bench/router-main-shim; PostgreSQL, Redis and Debian images by the same digests as in series 7. Three pairs; percentages of different pairs are never added or multiplied. With 3 pairs a nominal direction by chance is unlikely but possible; effects of the order of the aa-get-fast interval width are reported as uncertain.

scope: Series 8: the method of series 3 and 7 applied to two uvicorn settings of the optimized FastAPI variant (fastapi-msgspec): the HTTP protocol implementation (h11 versus httptools) and the access log (on versus off), plus the aa-get-fast noise reference. Request mix, generator, body verification, estimator and guards as in series 7.

platform_note: All runtime images and Go executables are amd64. msgspec is the official 0.22.0 PyPI wheel.
environment_guards: Pinned image IDs and source bindings; own container inventory before/after each point, lifecycle Docker events during main; host isolation guard at main start and end and at post start and end (API, PostgreSQL, Redis, sampler and generator on CPUs 0-3, NUMA node 0; Docker, containerd, user sessions, init and NIC interrupts on CPUs 4-7, NUMA node 1); stack probe (interpreter, package versions, router files, HTTP protocol module and access log lines) per variant in preflight.
duration_selection: Fixed 30/60 as in series 3 and 7; no result-dependent duration adjustment.
failure_policy: Any load error, missing telemetry, source/image change, foreign-container event or failed guard stops campaign; no retry or outlier exclusion.
